head_ref.description: The pull request's head branch; absent from older records.

coverage.description: Changed files no reviewer saw in full. Present only when one of its lists is not empty.

unavailable_sources.description: Changed files whose source the snapshot could not provide, so reviewers saw only their diff. A non-empty list makes the verdict INCOMPLETE unless findings request changes.

uncovered_files.description: Changed files no specialist covers, left unreviewed because the reviewer manifest sets uncovered to ignore. A deliberate opt-out: it does not change the verdict.

reviewers.description: The reviewers that ran: files covered, findings raised, reruns, and time taken.

model.description: The model the reviewer reported running on, from its accepted result; absent for a repository entrypoint reviewer and in older records.

seconds.description: Whole seconds from handing the role to a reviewer to its accepted result, reruns included; absent when the run was not timed.

patches.description: Each changed file's patch fingerprint, built from its added and removed lines only, so the next re-review can tell which files changed since; absent in older records.

scope.description: A re-review's scope: what was requested, what ran and why, and how much changed since the version it compared with. The changed counts are null when it could not compare.

repeats.description: Present only when the finding reports the same problem as another one, which it is counted with: a finding in this review (version equal to the record's) or the first finding of a ledger entry (an earlier version). Absent from records written before ledgers.

prior_dispositions.description: One per prior finding the review was given. In a record with a ledger, finding_id is the ledger entry's v<version>:<finding ID>; in an older record, a bare finding ID of the version it compared with.

ledger.description: Every problem raised on the pull request since its latest initial review, one entry each, ordered by version and finding ID. A re-review extends the latest record's ledger; an initial review starts a fresh one. Absent from records written before ledgers, which are read as having no history.

version.description: The review version where the problem first appeared.

id.description: Its finding ID in that version.

state.description: open when the latest judgment raised or repeated it or found it still_present or partially_addressed; closed when addressed or superseded; unverified when unable_to_verify. Open entries count toward the verdict.

judged_in.description: The version that last raised, repeated, or disposed of it.

dispositions.description: Each later review's disposition of it, oldest first.

repeats.description: The findings linked to it as repeats, oldest first.

github_comments.description: The open review comments the reviewers gave dispositions for, as listed in the request.
